meta.title: LordOS — the free, fast and secure Linux desktop
meta.description: LordOS is a free GNU/Linux distribution based on Debian with its own desktop environment, display server and Wayland compositor, built on solid Debian and Wayland foundations. Private by design. Runs on 64-bit PCs (amd64) and on the Raspberry Pi 5 (arm64).
meta.galleryDescription: Real screenshots of LordOS, the free GNU/Linux distribution based on Debian with a desktop environment of its own. No mockups, no retouching.

heroTitle: The free, fast and secure Linux desktop.
heroLead: LordOS is a free GNU/Linux distribution based on Debian with its own desktop environment, display server and Wayland compositor written in C, its own interface engine, and native apps made to feel calm, clear and private.
altDesktop: The LordOS desktop with the Dock, the menu bar and the About window
featTitle: Everything you need. Nothing you don’t.
featLead: A complete desktop with native apps, privacy built in, and the Linux apps you already use.
features: Its own display server and Wayland compositor in C and its own interface engine, on a solid Debian base. Smooth on any 64-bit PC (amd64), and light enough for the Raspberry Pi 5 (arm64).
Installable LordOS apps run isolated and ask before using your camera, microphone, files or network. You decide.
Watch every connection on a live world map, then allow or block it per app, or turn on blocklists of ad, tracker and malware sites.
A vault for passwords, 2FA codes and cards that unlocks with a password or a USB key.
Native apps for your accounts, with remote images blocked until you say so.
Chromium, Firefox and GTK apps fit right in, with the same window frame and dark mode.
showcase: CPU, memory, network, disks and now cooling: live temperatures, fan curves and a full-speed button for heavy work.
Monitor showing the Cooling tab with the fan curve
Categories, tags, a strong password generator and 2FA codes. The window is hidden from screenshots and screen sharing.
The Passwords app with an entry open
Dark mode, accent colors, the Dock on any side, displays, Bluetooth, energy and remote desktop, all in one place.
dlLead: Pay what you want, including nothing. Your support keeps LordOS free for everyone.
isoText: Live and installable ISOs: one for 64-bit PCs, and one for arm64 UEFI machines and virtual machines, so far run only on emulated QEMU. Try it without installing.
ovaText: A ready-made OVA for VirtualBox and VMware: import it, start it and create your account. No installer to run.
piText: A ready-to-flash image for SD card or NVMe, with fan control and our own kernel.
debText: Add LordOS to the system you already have, on a PC or a server (VPS), with one command:
imgText: Write LordOS to an SD card or a USB stick from the computer you already have, and set up the Raspberry Pi 5's first boot: its name, your account, Wi-Fi, remote access, appearance and cooling. Every official image is checked against the release signature before anything is erased.
imgNote: It also comes with LordOS (App Launcher → System). Free and open source, it collects nothing.
dlNote: Downloads are published on GitHub Releases with SHA-256 checksums.
verifyText: Every release is signed with the LordOS release key. Check the signature before you install. Key fingerprint (SHA-256):
supLead: LordOS is free and open source. If it makes your computer better, help us keep building it.
payNote: With Mercado Pago you choose the amount on the next page.
lumoText: Lumo is a small celestial fox with white fur and violet highlights. Its crown and cape stand for protection, freedom and control, and it shows up when something needs your attention.
aboutLead: LordOS is created by the iPERFEX group, by Pablo Miranda and Federico Pereira.

pi.metaTitle: LordOS on the Raspberry Pi 5 and Raspberry Pi 500
pi.metaDescription: A full desktop on the Raspberry Pi 5 and Pi 500: GPU-composed, hardware video decoding, fan control and the Argon ONE V5 case, with numbers from real boards.
pi.title: A full desktop on your Raspberry Pi
pi.lead: LordOS draws its desktop on the Pi's GPU, decodes HEVC video in hardware, drives the fan and knows the Argon ONE V5 case by name. One image for both boards, written with LordOS Imager.
pi.capArgon: Raspberry Pi 5 in the Argon ONE V5 case

pi.artPi5: Drawing of the Raspberry Pi 5 board
pi.testedLead: Numbers from the reports LordOS makes itself ({cmd} and About LordOS), not from a spec sheet.
pi5Rows: 56 MB of RAM, a frame in 5.8 ms
Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, USB audio, Wi-Fi, Ethernet
pi500Rows: 1.8 GB of 7.9 GB, browser and Mail open
The built-in keyboard, recognized as is
pi.argonTitle: The Argon ONE V5 case, supported
pi.argonText: LordOS finds the case on the first boot and asks you once. After that, Settings → Cooling drives its blower with LordOS's own fan service, and its front USB ports and audio jack work. No vendor scripts.
argonPoints: the aluminium body is a big heatsink. With Balanced, the fan stayed off at 50–53 °C under a full four-core load.
2,700 RPM at 30 %, 4,500 at 55 %, up to 7,400 at full speed.
two USB 2.0 ports, microphone and headphones, on after you pick the case in Settings and restart.
LordOS never changes the bootloader's power settings.

pi.toolsLead: They come with LordOS, work over SSH too, and never send anything on their own.
tools: The crown and a one-screen summary: version, board, kernel, display, CPU, GPU, memory, disk and isolation. --share hides your user and computer names for a screenshot.

A complete report for a bug or a hardware test: devices, drivers, displays, signed code, failed services and this boot's errors. Names and addresses are replaced; it only reads, and saves a file you check before posting.
System Information from a terminal: report for the hardware, and bench --quick or --full for LordBench, the same measurements as the app, also as JSON.
A test card in a window: frames a second and frame times, every key lit as you press it, the mouse and its wheel, and what the display server reports. Handy to check a new keyboard, mouse or screen.
pi.shareTitle: Tried LordOS on your Pi? Tell us
pi.shareText: Every report helps the next person: which board, which case, which screen, what worked. LordOS writes the report for you, with names and addresses removed, and changes nothing.
pi.shareAlt: Or open System Information → Compatibility and share it from there.
pi.shareGithub: Send a hardware report on GitHub
pi.benchLead: LordOS comes with its own benchmark. It waits for a quiet system, measures the CPU, memory, GPU, the compositor and video, and compares your board with our reference Raspberry Pi 5.
benchSteps: Open System Information → Performance and press Quick test (under a minute). The Full test adds the disk, every video codec and a few minutes of load on all cores: 4 to 6 minutes, with some wear on an SD card.
Run the same tests over SSH, also as JSON:
Post a screenshot of the Performance tab on r/LordOS, or paste the JSON in a hardware report, with your board, case and power supply. That is how we see where LordOS is fast and where it isn't yet.
